intended_object: The coordinate Hopf algebra O(H) over a commutative ring A of the closed subgroup scheme H ⊆ GL₅₆ generated by the 14 root subgroups (for the ± simple roots) and the split weight torus of the E₇ minuscule (56-dimensional) representation. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition is the quotient of O(GL₅₆) = A[x_ij, det⁻¹] by `generatedDefiningIdeal A`. That ideal is `commonKernelHopfIdeal (generatorCoordinateMap A)`, the supremum of all Hopf ideals that lie in the kernel of every generator coordinate map. These maps are O(GL₅₆) → O(𝔾ₐ) for the 14 root subgroups and O(GL₅₆) → O(split torus) for the weight torus.

Under the anti-equivalence between closed subgroup schemes of GL₅₆ and Hopf ideals of O(GL₅₆), the largest Hopf ideal in all these kernels corresponds to the smallest closed subgroup scheme through which every generator morphism factors. That is exactly the closed subgroup generated by the root subgroups and the torus, in the sense of Humphreys §§26–27 and Milne §2.h, which the module cites.

Taking the sup over Hopf ideals, rather than intersecting the kernels as ring ideals, is the right choice: an intersection of kernels need not be a Hopf ideal, and its quotient would only be the closure of the union of the images, not a subgroup.

The ring A is an arbitrary commutative ring, which is the natural generality for this specific group scheme. The dimension 56, the index type Sum (Fin 7 ⊕ Fin 7) Unit and the E₇ data are part of what the object is, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no such object.
